key_insight: A neural topology optimization method using KATO can design ship structures with lower forced-vibration active input power while keeping layouts connected and manufacturable.
engineering_relevance: This enables lighter, feature-controlled ship panels and foundations that better resist propulsion-induced vibrations, noise, fatigue, and equipment damage.
method: Uses a convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KATO) to parameterize topology optimization.
Optimizes active input power (AIP) under forced vibration, with Helmholtz filtering and Heaviside projection for feature-size control.
Benchmarks against GCMMA and evaluates multiple ship-structure cases, including near-resonant behavior and stress-aware designs.
evidence_signal: Across deck and frame cases, KATO reduced AIP relative to size-optimized references, matched GCMMA within 0.5 dB in frame variants, and in a near-resonant case cut peak AIP by more than 32 dB while improving static compliance and runtime.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful filtering, projection, and matched-volume re-analysis; near-resonant optimization can still be sensitive to formulation and manufacturing constraints.
paper_title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
